evidence: The chemical compositions of the IGZO films were examined by X-ray fluorescence (XRF, ZSX Primus II, Rigaku, Japan) spectroscopy, for which the atomic concentration was calibrated by proton-induced X-ray emission. The structural properties of the IGZO films were evaluated by glancing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD, SmartLab, Rigaku, Japan) using Cu Kα radiation (40 kV, 30 mA) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM, JEM-2100F, JEOL, Japan). Also, atomic force microscopy (AFM, Multimode 8, Bruker) was used to determine the surface roughness of the IGZO films. The thickness and band gap of the films were measured using spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE, Elli-SE, Ellipso Technology, South Korea). Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS, Theta Probe, Thermo Fisher Scientific) was carried out using an excitation source of HeI of 21.2 eV to analyze the Fermi level against the valence band (VB) maximum and work function. The chemical properties of the IGZO films were examined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, KAlpha+, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with an X-ray source of monochromatic Al Kα of 1486.6 eV. The carrier density (ne) and Hall mobility (μHall) were evaluated through Hall effect measurements with a van der Pauw configuration.
